result.instructions: Logimu shopping data — Amazon (US, UK, DE, CA, AU, FR, IT, ES, JP, MX, BR) & Walmart US: curated product search with ranked shortlists (shopping), single-ASIN dossiers with price/stock/BSR/offer history plus observed product-page content (product, which also resolves GTIN/UPC/EAN barcodes), warehouse filtering (search), live Amazon and Walmart search-page fetches (serp — real-time, takes seconds), live Walmart product pages (product with country=walmart and mode=live), live Amazon Best Sellers lists by category (bestsellers — up to 100 ranked products plus the category tree), live offers pages (offers — every seller of a product right now: price, condition, buy box, FBA/FBM, by ASIN or barcode) and live Amazon Today's Deals (deals — deal and list price, % off, lightning deals with % claimed and end time, filtered by department, deal type, discount and price). Fresh observed data (prices, stock, real ratings), no affiliate bias. Without signup only shopping works: 5 ranked searches per day, without detail. Product records and history, warehouse search, live scrapes, tracking and bulk/scheduled batch jobs need a paid plan: the user signs in with their Logimu account (OAuth: Claude shows a Connect card, or asks at setup) or passes an API key (plans from $19/month, https://api.logimu.com) as a Bearer token; calls are credit-metered, and misses/empty results are never billed. Paid plans add product records and history, warehouse search, seller profiles, brand / category intelligence, keyword suggestions and keyword rankings (which products show on page 1 of a search, which keywords a product shows up for, and where competitors appear and it does not).

asin.description: 10-character Amazon ASIN, or a numeric Walmart item ID when country=walmart. Provide either asin or gtin.

gtin.description: GTIN / UPC / EAN barcode (12, 13 or 14 digits; punctuation and leading zeros are tolerated), resolved to an ASIN in the requested marketplace. USE WHEN the user gives a barcode instead of an ASIN — scanned off a package, from a supplier sheet, or copied from a listing. A barcode can legitimately map to several ASINs; the best match is returned and the rest are listed in gtin_matches. Never billed when the barcode is unknown to us.

country.description: Marketplace to look the product up in. Amazon: us, uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx, br. walmart = Walmart US (United States only). Pick the marketplace matching the user's country or locale when known (a German user -> de, a Canadian user -> ca); default us.

mode.description: cache = stored observation only; live = force an on-demand scrape (Amazon only, takes a few seconds); auto = serve cache when fresher than max_age_days, otherwise scrape.

max_age_days.description: How old a cached observation may be before mode=auto triggers a live scrape.

include_used.description: Include used, refurbished, open-box and collectible offers in current_sellers (default false keeps the new-condition list). Every seller row always carries condition (the marketplace's own label) and condition_class (new, used_like_new, used_very_good, used_good, used_acceptable, used, refurbished, open_box, collectible, unknown); current_sellers always carries used_offer_count, lowest_new (the cheapest new offer - the list is buy-box first, not price-sorted) and lowest_used (the cheapest second-hand offer) even without opting in. With offer_history it returns one series per seller+condition_class. Cached, live and historical data alike; not billed extra.

offer_history.description: Attach the buy-box owner timeline and per-seller daily price series (US buy-box depth back to Dec 2024) plus buybox_price_history, the lowest buy-box price of every observed day (Amazon US back to Nov 2023). Amazon marketplaces only; needs a paid-plan API key (from $19/mo). Included in the record, no extra credits.

history_sellers.description: With offer_history: how many of the most-observed sellers carry a point series (default 10, max 50). Every observed seller is always listed as a summary row with points_total.

history_points.description: With offer_history: points per series, the most recent N observed days (default 500, max 20,000). Wider series are included too, no extra credits (offer_history.points_extra still reports the points beyond the default 10 x 500).

bsr_history.description: Attach the full per-category BSR rank history (era-tagged daily points back to Oct 2023 for US; legacy top-100 segments are flagged censored). Amazon marketplaces only; needs a paid-plan API key (from $19/mo). Included in the record, no extra credits.

history_only.description: Return ONLY the stored history series - bsr_history, offer_history and buybox_price_history - with no snapshot, content or seller table, for 0.05 credit. USE WHEN the user tracks price or rank over time for many products and does not need the current listing. Amazon marketplaces only, served from stored observations (mode=live is refused); needs a paid-plan API key (from $19/mo).

track.description: Answer AND track (paid plans): after this answer the ASIN is pinned into our hot lane, which re-reads its all-offers page (or, with read=product_page, its product page) every `interval` for 30 days and adds every read to buybox_price_points_hot - the same as the track_product tool. No extra credits (the plan's daily tracked-snapshot allowance is drawn); the answer is served even when the tracking is refused and its `track` block says why. Amazon only.

interval.description: With track=true: how often the lane re-reads the product (1h = 24 snapshots a day).

read.description: With track=true (2026-10-29): offers (default) re-reads the all-offers page; product_page re-reads the product page and its offers page, so every reading's sales rank lands in bsr_points_hot. A product-page read draws 2 snapshots of the allowance.

q.description: What to search for, e.g. 'coffee maker'. Literal keywords, not semantic: every term must match, so extra or inferred words only narrow the result set. Query in the marketplace's own language - there is no translation. A bare ASIN returns exactly that product.

country.description: Marketplace to search. Amazon: us, uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx, br. walmart = Walmart US (United States only). Pick the marketplace matching the user's country or locale when known (a German user -> de, a Canadian user -> ca); default us. Prices are returned in that marketplace's local currency.

group.description: How to group the shortlist. auto = choose category or price tiers automatically; category = group by product category; price = group into Budget/Mid-range/Premium; none = one flat ranked list.

min_price.description: Minimum price, in the marketplace's local currency. USE WHEN the user sets a floor ('at least £50', 'nothing cheap').

max_price.description: Maximum price, in the marketplace's local currency. USE WHEN the user gives a budget or says cheap/affordable/under X — pass the number here rather than putting the word in q, where it is matched as a literal word in the product title and throws away real results.

brand.description: Restrict to one exact brand. USE WHEN the user names a brand they want ('Anker charger'); prefer this over putting the brand in q.

format.description: Books/media only: return only this format - kindle, paperback, hardcover, mass_market, audiobook, audio_cd, board_book, spiral, library_binding or other (comma-separate several). USE WHEN the user wants a specific edition ('LOTR in paperback', 'the audiobook').

collapse.description: true (default): one row per book, its other formats listed in the row's `formats` (each with its own ASIN and price). false: every format as its own row.

include_unavailable.description: false (default): only products with a current offer, so the shortlist is buyable. true: also list items that currently have NO offer on the marketplace (Amazon 'Currently unavailable': price null, in_stock false). USE WHEN the user asks about a specific discontinued or sold-out product; otherwise leave it off.

sort.description: relevance (default) | price (cheapest first) | rating. USE price when the user asks for the cheapest, rating when they ask for the best-reviewed.

detail.description: Attach per-product intelligence to every product returned (30-day price and stock change events, full stock history and state, bought-past-month badge, current sellers). Keyed accounts only. 5 credits per query instead of 2.

q.description: Keyword matched against the product title. Acts as the anchor when brand is not given. Literal keywords, not semantic: every term must match, so extra or inferred words only narrow the result set. Query in the marketplace's own language — there is no translation.

brand.description: Exact brand name. Acts as the anchor when q is not given.

seller.description: Restrict to products this seller has been observed offering. REFINEMENT ONLY - cannot be used on its own; pair it with an anchor (q, brand, or category).

category.description: A department or sub-category name (e.g. 'Home & Kitchen', 'Beading Storage'), matched in full and case-insensitively against the product's category chain — comma-separate several. Works BOTH ways: as an ANCHOR on its own to browse a category with no keyword ('everything in Home & Kitchen under $30, most reviews first'), or as a REFINEMENT alongside q or brand. A category-only browse returns the category's top products by in-category best-seller rank, then applies your filters and sort.

marketplace.description: Which tracked marketplace to query. walmart = Walmart US (United States only). Pick the marketplace matching the user's country or locale when known; default amazon-us.

price_min.description: Minimum current price, in the marketplace's local currency.

price_max.description: Maximum current price, in the marketplace's local currency.

rating_max.description: Maximum average star rating. USE WHEN looking for products whose reviews are weak — an incumbent rated 3.2 is an opening.

seller_count_min.description: Minimum number of sellers competing on the listing. USE WHEN the user wants proven demand rather than an untested listing.

seller_count_max.description: Maximum number of sellers competing on the listing. USE WHEN the user asks for products with little competition, few sellers, or an easy listing to win — this is the core sourcing filter.

fbm.description: Only merchant-fulfilled listings. The counterpart of fba, which was already exposed.

rating_min.description: Minimum star rating, on a 0-5 scale.

bsr_min.description: Minimum Best Sellers Rank. Lower BSR means stronger sales, so this excludes the best sellers.

bsr_max.description: Maximum Best Sellers Rank. Use this to keep only strong sellers.

fba.description: true = only Fulfilled by Amazon offers, false = only merchant-fulfilled. Omit to include both.

fulfillment.description: Buy-box fulfilment of the listing: amz = sold by Amazon itself, fba = a third party fulfilled by Amazon, fbm = merchant-fulfilled. Finer than fba/fbm because it separates Amazon Retail from FBA sellers. Amazon marketplaces only.

sort.description: Field to order results by. bsr sorts ascending (best sellers first); the others sort descending.

max_per_category.description: Cap how many results may come from any one category, to spread results across categories.

name.description: Instead of seller_id: the seller's display name as Amazon prints it (e.g. 'Total Office Solutions'). Resolved through observed buy-box data to the seller id; a name we have never observed, or one with no id on record, returns guidance - nothing is billed.

country.description: Amazon marketplace. No Walmart - seller pages are Amazon-only.

mode.description: Profile lane (see description). products=true uses products_mode.

max_age_days.description: auto only: how old the stored observation may be before fetching live (default 14 = the tracker's cadence).

history.description: Also return history{} (rating + storefront-size change points, oldest first, UTC). +0.5 credit when non-empty.

history_points.description: history=true: the latest N change points per series (1-5000).

products.description: Also return the seller's products (billed separately, see description).

products_mode.description: cache = observed products (fast); live = the storefront now (seconds).

page.description: Products page (cache: 25 per page; live: Amazon's page 1-10).

max_page.description: live products only: auto-paginate up to this page (max 10); billed per page fetched.

brands.description: Also return the operator footprint: brands this seller was observed winning the buy box on (16 months), 25 per page (brands_page). +1 credit per page.

network.description: Also return connected sellers: sellers winning the buy box on the same brands, strongest overlap first (max 50). +1 credit.

q.description: The search query, exactly as a shopper would type it into Amazon's search box. Query in the marketplace's own language.

country.description: Amazon marketplace to search, or walmart (a live walmart.com search).

max_page.description: Auto-paginate page..max_page and concatenate (positions stay continuous across pages). Max 10 pages per request; billed per page actually fetched.

sort_by.description: Amazon's own sort orders; default is Amazon's Featured.

category_id.description: Amazon browse-node id to scope the search (becomes &node=).

refinements.description: Amazon rh= refinement value. Round-trips: feed back any refinements[*].value from a previous serp response.

exclude_sponsored.description: Drop inline sponsored results. Often a no-op — Amazon usually keeps paid placements in separate carousels outside the organic grid.

zip.description: Optional (2026-10-29): a US 5-digit ZIP - the search as a shopper at that ZIP sees it, with the local stores' items, each result's store, delivery_terms and stock, and the page's confirmed location. country=us only; at most 3 pages a call. A verified empty answer (empty_reason set) is billed 1 credit. ZIP+4 is cut to 5 digits.

store.description: Optional, with zip only: Amazon's own storefront search for that store's assortment at the ZIP (Whole Foods Market or Amazon Fresh). A local partner such as Lucky is reached through refinements with its p_n_alm_brand_id value. Cannot be combined with category_id.

url.description: An Amazon Best Sellers URL: a category (e.g. https://www.amazon.com/gp/bestsellers/kitchen/289814, or any URL from a previous answer's subcategories / categories / path) or a marketplace's root (https://www.amazon.de/gp/bestsellers/). The marketplace comes from the host.

country.description: Without url: that marketplace's root list of top-level categories (start here when you have no URL yet). With url: must match the URL's marketplace.

pages.description: 1 = ranks 1-50 (1 credit), 2 = ranks 1-100 (default, 2 credits). Ignored for the root list.

asin.description: The product's 10-character Amazon ASIN (a print book's ISBN-10 works too). Provide asin or gtin.

gtin.description: A barcode instead of an ASIN: UPC-12, EAN-13, GTIN-14 or ISBN-13. Resolved cheapest evidence first: a listing we observe that carries it, a book's ISBN-10, the same product on another Amazon marketplace, then Amazon's own search (organic results only). gtin_resolution says which, and barcode_verified whether the listing itself carries the barcode. A barcode nothing resolves is never billed.

country.description: The Amazon marketplace to read the offers page on.

include_used.description: true also lists the used, refurbished, open-box and collectible offers in current_sellers.sellers. Either way current_sellers carries used_offer_count, lowest_new and lowest_used, and every row its condition. Not billed extra.

zip.description: Optional (2026-10-14): a US 5-digit ZIP - the offers page as Amazon shows it to a shopper at that ZIP, with location (Amazon's confirmed 'Deliver to' answer) and deliverable (whether the item is offered to that ZIP right now; Amazon Fresh and Whole Foods items deliver only to some ZIPs, and an out-of-area ZIP shows the same unavailable box as a stock-out). Page 1 of the offers only, a one-off session, nothing stored. country=us only. 1 credit when the answer carries an offer, and (since 2026-10-29) for a verified not-deliverable answer (the ZIP confirmed on the page, the offers page read, zero offers: not_deliverable_verified true); a ZIP Amazon rejects is guidance, never billed, as are deliverable null, a 404 and a failed fetch. A session at a ZIP is kept a few minutes per account, so this check right after a serp zip= search on the same ZIP skips the warm-up.

country.description: The Amazon marketplace whose deals page to read. Required unless url is given; with url it must match the URL's marketplace.

url.description: Optional: an Amazon deals URL (/deals, /events/deals or /gp/goldbox). The host decides the marketplace and its query string is kept (e.g. a filtered deals page copied from the browser).

category_id.description: A deals department id from categories[] of a previous answer (Amazon applies one department at a time).

deal_types.description: One of Amazon's stable deal collections. Not together with collection.

collection.description: Any other collection id from collections[] of a previous answer (collections differ per marketplace and over time). Not together with deal_types.

discount.description: Rainforest form of min_discount (50_percent_off = at least 50% off). Not together with min_discount.

min_discount.description: Minimum percent off (0-100). Amazon applies it on the us, uk, de, ca, au, mx, jp and br deals pages; amazon.it, amazon.fr and amazon.es have no discount filter, so there it is refused (not_applied, never billed): ask without it and filter on percent_off.

max_discount.description: Maximum percent off (0-100). Same marketplaces as min_discount (refused on it, fr, es).

min_price.description: Minimum deal price in the marketplace currency (Amazon applies whole units; a fraction is rounded down).

max_price.description: Maximum deal price in the marketplace currency (Amazon applies whole units; a fraction is rounded up).

minimum_rating.description: Only products rated at least this many stars (1-4).

brand.description: A brand id from facets.brands of a previous answer (e.g. 811979|dreame).

page_size.description: Deals per page; Amazon serves steps of 30 only. Every page is 1 credit whatever its size, so 120 gives the most deals per credit.

pages.description: Consecutive pages merged into one answer, starting at page (stops early on a short page). 1 credit per page that returned deals.

brand.description: Brand name as Amazon prints it (case-insensitive).

history.description: Add history.monthly (up to 24 months). +0.5 credit when non-empty.

sellers.description: Add the full seller list (25 per page). +1 credit per page.

network.description: Add the seller map: connected brands + weighted edges. +1 credit.

category_id.description: Logimu category id (warehouse id, as returned by every search result and listing).

node_id.description: Instead of category_id: the Amazon browse-node id.

q.description: Instead of an id: part of a category name or path (English alias included) - returns candidate categories, free.

list.description: Walk the taxonomy: the marketplace's root categories, or the children of parent_id. Free.

parent_id.description: With list=true: list this category's children instead of the roots.

category_id.description: top_brands: root category id to narrow to.

parent_id.description: top_categories: list this category's children instead of roots.

seed.description: A seed term or prefix, at least 3 characters, e.g. 'electric toothbrush'.

country.description: Amazon marketplace (ignored when compare is given).

history.description: Also return each list's observation history (+0.5 credit when a closed observation exists).

compare.description: Comma-separated marketplaces to compare instead of one lookup, e.g. 'us,uk,de' (2-11).

keyword.description: A search term, e.g. 'micro sd card 128gb high endurance' (case-insensitive).

country.description: Amazon marketplace: us (amazon.com, default), uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx or br, each searched in its own language. us and uk are read in full about weekly; the other nine started 2026-10-29 / 10-30 and fill in week by week (coverage says how far).

history.description: Also return every weekly observation and the products' rank series; +0.5 credit when more than one exists.

asin.description: A 10-character Amazon ASIN: the keywords it shows up for. Give asin OR asins.

asins.description: Up to 10 ASINs, the product first, then the competitors to compare it with.

country.description: Amazon marketplace: us (amazon.com, default), uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx or br, each searched in its own language. us and uk are read in full about weekly; the other nine started 2026-10-29 / 10-30 and fill in week by week (coverage says how far).

placement.description: Organic and sponsored (default), organic only, or sponsored only.

gaps.description: With asins: only the keywords where a competitor is on page 1 organically and the first product is not.

limit.description: Keywords per answer (1 credit per 25 returned, per ASIN).

history.description: Also return the first product's rank on each keyword in every observation; +0.5 credit when a keyword has more than one.

action.description: track (default) creates or renews the tracking(s); stop ends one or many at once; sync (2026-10-14) makes the account's active set on one marketplace EQUAL to asins: missing ones are created, active ones not listed are stopped, the rest are left as they are - dry_run first to see the counts.

id.description: With action=stop: the tracking id (from list_tracked). Or give asin + country, or ids / asins.

ids.description: With action=stop: several tracking ids at once (up to 10,000).

asin.description: The product's 10-character Amazon ASIN (one product). Or give asins.

asins.description: Bulk (2026-10-14): up to 10,000 ASINs in one call - with action=track all get the same interval / ttl_days / alerts (results[] in input order: created / renewed / refused / invalid, the allowance consumed in input order, never all-or-nothing); with action=stop they are stopped; with action=sync they are the full list the active set becomes.

dry_run.description: With action=sync: return what would be created and stopped without writing.

country.description: The Amazon marketplace to track the product on.

interval.description: How often the lane re-reads the product (see read). A shorter interval costs more of the daily allowance (1h = 24 snapshots a day, 2h = 12, 4h = 6, 12h = 2, 24h = 1; twice that with read=product_page).

read.description: Which page each read fetches (2026-10-29): offers (default) = the all-offers page (buy box, price, every offer, stock); product_page = the product page and its offers page, so the sales rank is read too: every reading lands in the product tool's bsr_points_hot, and its offers page in buybox_price_points_hot as with offers. A product-page read draws 2 snapshots of the allowance (12h = 4 a day). Like interval, every call sets it: tracking the same ASIN again without read switches it back to offers.

ttl_days.description: Optional: stop after this many days (1-365). Omit (or 0) and the tracking runs for as long as the plan is active - a lapsed plan keeps it 7 days, then it pauses and resumes with the plan.

alert_email.description: Optional: e-mail alerts for the notify_if thresholds - 'true' for the account's own address, or an address. One e-mail per event, at most 50 a day per tracking. 'false' detaches. Works with or without webhook_url.

webhook_url.description: Optional: an https URL Logimu POSTs to when a notify_if threshold fires on a new observation (signed X-Logimu-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, body); the secret is returned once in webhook_secret). An empty string detaches it.

notify_if.description: With webhook_url and / or alert_email: the thresholds. price_below / price_above (a buy-box price), price_change_pct (percent move of the buy-box price since the last in-stock read), buybox_seller_change (true: a different seller holds the buy box, between two in-stock reads), offer_count_below / offer_count_above (a count), availability_change (true: the stock STATE changed - in_stock, no_buybox = offers exist but Amazon shows no featured offer, out_of_stock = no offers at all, confirmed by a second read; the event carries both codes), out_of_stock (true: shorthand for a change to out_of_stock), back_in_stock (true: a change to in_stock). {} attaches the webhook and fires on nothing.

country.description: Only this marketplace's trackings (default: every marketplace).

status.description: Only trackings in this state (default: all, newest first).

asin.description: Only these products: one ASIN or up to 500 comma-separated (2026-10-30).

offset.description: Rows to skip (paging; total says how many there are).

events_for.description: A tracking id: return that tracking's webhook events instead of the list - which notify_if threshold fired on which observation, the payload, and the delivery state (pending / delivered / failed, attempts, last error).

action.description: What to do (see the tool description).

batch_id.description: For run / status / results / schedule / delete.

run_id.description: For status (one run's progress) and results.

kind.description: estimate / create: product (default), search, seller, brand, category, keywords, or any endpoint kind named in the description.

country.description: estimate / create: us, uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx, br, walmart (search batches Amazon only).

mode.description: product / seller batches: cache = warehouse only, live = scrape every row, auto = warehouse when fresh enough (required on create for product batches).

asins.description: product batches: the ASINs (or Walmart item ids).

gtins.description: product batches: barcodes instead of ASINs.

source.description: product batches: tracked = the ASINs this account tracks on the marketplace instead of a list.

terms.description: search / shopping / warehouse_search / category_search batches: the queries.

category_ids.description: category / categories batches (ids, or root); deals batches (deals department ids, or all for the whole deals page).

pages.description: search batches: pages per term (1-3); ranked-list batches: pages of 25 rows (1-40).

params.description: endpoint kinds: the endpoint's query parameters, fixed for every row.

include.description: Extras: history (seller / brand / category / keywords), reviews, used, offer_history, bsr_history, history_only (product), blocks (search).

start.description: create: also launch the first run at once.

schedule.description: schedule: how often the batch re-runs (none stops the schedule). 12h fires twice a day, at at_hour_utc and 12 hours later; daily once a day at at_hour_utc (default midnight UTC); weekly on Monday and monthly on the 1st, 00:00 UTC.

at_hour_utc.description: schedule, 12h and daily only: the UTC hour it fires at (12h: this hour and 12 hours later). Default: 12h = the current UTC hour, daily = 0. Kept when the same cadence is saved again without it.

credit_ceiling.description: schedule: a firing whose fresh estimate exceeds this does not run (email instead); default 2x the estimate.

webhook_url.description: schedule: POSTed on run completion / pause, HMAC-SHA256 signed; the secret is returned once.

email.description: create / schedule: e-mail the account when a run completes or pauses and when a scheduled firing is refused. Default false for batches created here or through the REST API; results are always available programmatically.

limit.description: results: rows to return (page with offset; the download URLs carry everything).

results.category: Electronics > Audio & Home Theatre > Radios & Boomboxes > Boomboxes > Portable Speakers
results.description:
Take big JBL Pro sound wherever you go. The bold, colorful JBL Go 4 ultra-portable Bluetooth speaker fits in the palm of your hand, delivering clear, loud JBL Pro Sound with rich, punchy bass. Its newly redesigned integrated loop makes it easy to bring anywhere, and the variety of colorways means you can choose one that fits your vibe. Plus it's waterproof and dustproof, so it loves to go outside. And up to 7 hours of playtime mean it will keep the good times rolling throughout a fun day trip or an evening chilling under the stars. Pair two Go 4s for stereo sound, or wirelessly connect multiple JBL Auracast-enabled speakers for even bigger sound. Crank it up and let your music take you anywhere.
